testName: IISER IAT Mock Test: Moving Charges and Magnetism (Version 1)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle of mass m and charge q enters a uniform magnetic field B perpendicularly and moves in a circular path. What is the total work done by the magnetic force on the particle over one complete revolution?
questions.explanation: The magnetic force F = q(v × B) is always perpendicular to the velocity vector v. Since power P = F · v = 0, the magnetic force does no work on the particle. Hence, the work done over any path, including a complete revolution, is strictly zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Which of the following equations correctly represents the Biot-Savart law in vector form for the magnetic field dB due to a current element Idl at a position vector r?
questions.explanation: The Biot-Savart law gives the magnetic field dB due to a current element Idl. In vector form, it is dB = (μ₀ I / 4π) * (dl × r̂) / r². Substituting the unit vector r̂ = r / r yields dB = (μ₀ I / 4π) * (dl × r) / r³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two long, straight, parallel wires carry steady currents in the same direction. Which of the following statements about the magnetic force between them is true?
options: The wires attract each other because the magnetic fields produced by them cancel out.
The wires repel each other due to the Lorentz force.
The wires attract each other due to the Lorentz force acting on moving charges.
The wires experience zero net force because they are uncharged.
questions.explanation: Parallel wires carrying currents in the same direction attract each other. This is fundamentally due to the Lorentz magnetic force (F = I(l × B)) acting on the charges moving in one wire due to the magnetic field generated by the other wire.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long ideal solenoid has n turns per unit length and carries a current I, producing a magnetic field B at its center. If the current is halved and the number of turns per unit length is doubled, what will be the new magnetic field at the center of the solenoid?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field at the center of an ideal long solenoid is given by B = μ₀ n I. Let the initial field be B₁ = μ₀ n I. The new number of turns per unit length is n' = 2n, and the new current is I' = I/2. The new magnetic field is B₂ = μ₀ (2n) (I/2) = μ₀ n I = B. The field remains unchanged.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: In order to convert a moving coil galvanometer into an ammeter capable of measuring large currents, one must connect:
options: A high resistance in parallel with the galvanometer.
A low resistance in series with the galvanometer.
A high resistance in series with the galvanometer.
A low resistance in parallel with the galvanometer.
questions.explanation: To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter, a low resistance called a shunt must be connected in parallel with the galvanometer coil. This allows the majority of the main circuit current to bypass the sensitive galvanometer coil.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A circular current loop of area A and current I is placed in a uniform magnetic field B. What is the maximum magnitude of the torque that the magnetic field can exert on the loop?
questions.explanation: The torque on a current loop is given by τ = M × B, where M = IA. The magnitude of the torque is τ = I A B sin(θ). The maximum torque occurs when the plane of the loop is parallel to the magnetic field (θ = 90° between the area vector and the B-field). Thus, τ_max = I A B.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A moving coil galvanometer has a rectangular coil of 50 turns, each with an area of 2 × 10⁻⁴ m². The coil is suspended in a radial magnetic field of 0.02 T. The torsional constant of the suspension wire is 10⁻⁴ N·m/rad. The resistance of the galvanometer coil is 100 Ω. What is the current sensitivity of this galvanometer?
questions.explanation: Current sensitivity I_S = φ/I = NAB/k. Substituting N = 50, A = 2 × 10⁻⁴, B = 0.02, k = 10⁻⁴ yields I_S = (50 × 2 × 10⁻⁴ × 0.02) / 10⁻⁴ = 0.0002 / 10⁻⁴ = 2 rad/A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Using the data from the previous question, what is the voltage sensitivity of this galvanometer?
questions.explanation: Voltage sensitivity V_S = I_S / R. From the previous question, I_S = 2 rad/A. The coil resistance R = 100 Ω. V_S = 2 / 100 = 0.02 rad/V.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: The galvanometer described previously shows a full-scale deflection for a current of 10 mA. If a shunt resistance of 1 Ω is connected across the galvanometer to convert it into an ammeter, what is the new maximum current (full-scale range) of the ammeter?
questions.explanation: Using the shunt formula: I_g * R_g = (I - I_g) * S. Substituting I_g = 0.01 A, R_g = 100 Ω, S = 1 Ω. We get 0.01 × 100 = (I - 0.01) × 1. This gives 1 = I - 0.01, so I = 1.01 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A straight wire carrying a current I is bent into a semi-circular arc of radius R. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the center of the arc?
questions.explanation: The magnetic field at the center of a complete circular loop is B = μ₀I / 2R. A semi-circular arc subtends exactly half the angle of a full circle. By Biot-Savart law integration, the field is exactly half that of a full loop. B_semi = 1/2 * (μ₀I / 2R) = μ₀I / 4R.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A proton and an alpha particle enter a uniform magnetic field perpendicularly with the exact same kinetic energy. The field is directed into the plane of the paper. Let r_p and r_α be the radii of their respective circular trajectories. What is the ratio r_p : r_α?
questions.explanation: The radius of a charged particle in a magnetic field is r = mv/qB = √(2mK) / qB. For a proton: r_p = √(2m_p K) / eB. For an alpha particle: m_α = 4m_p, q_α = 2e. r_α = √(2(4m_p)K) / 2eB = 2√(2m_p K) / 2eB = √(2m_p K) / eB. Thus, r_p : r_α = 1 : 1.
questions.imagePrompt: A clean, academic diagram showing a uniform magnetic field directed into the page (represented by crosses). Two distinct curved trajectories, labeled 'Proton' and 'Alpha particle', enter the magnetic field perpendicularly from the bottom. They both trace exact semi-circular paths of the same radius before exiting. The background is white, suitable for a physics textbook.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long, straight solid cylindrical conductor of radius R carries a steady current I that is uniformly distributed across its cross-section. Let B₁ be the magnetic field at a radial distance r = R/2 from the axis, and B₂ be the magnetic field at a radial distance r = 2R from the axis. What is the ratio B₁ / B₂?
questions.explanation: For a solid cylinder, inside (r < R): B = μ₀Ir / 2πR². At r = R/2, B₁ = μ₀I(R/2) / 2πR² = μ₀I / 4πR. Outside (r > R): B = μ₀I / 2πr. At r = 2R, B₂ = μ₀I / 2π(2R) = μ₀I / 4πR. The ratio B₁ / B₂ is 1.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A straight current-carrying wire of length L carries a steady current I along the positive x-axis. It is placed in a uniform magnetic field given by B = B₀(î + ĵ + k̂). What is the magnitude of the magnetic force experienced by the wire?
questions.explanation: Magnetic force on a straight wire is F = I(L × B). Current vector L = Lî. Magnetic field B = B₀(î + ĵ + k̂). F = I (Lî) × B₀(î + ĵ + k̂) = ILB₀ [î × î + î × ĵ + î × k̂] = ILB₀ [0 + k̂ - ĵ]. The magnitude of the force is |F| = ILB₀ √((1)² + (-1)²) = √2 I L B₀.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A rectangular loop carrying a clockwise steady current I lies entirely in the xy-plane. A uniform magnetic field B points entirely in the positive x-direction. What is the direction of the torque vector acting on the loop?
questions.explanation: Torque τ = μ × B. The current loop is in the xy-plane and flows clockwise. By the right-hand rule, the magnetic dipole moment μ points into the page (negative z-direction): μ = -IAk̂. The magnetic field is B = Bî. τ = (-IAk̂) × (Bî) = -IAB (k̂ × î). Since k̂ × î = ĵ, we get τ = -IABĵ. The torque acts in the negative y-direction.
questions.imagePrompt: A 3D schematic of a rectangular current loop in the x-y plane, carrying a clockwise current I. The x, y, and z axes are clearly labeled. A set of straight, parallel arrows indicates a uniform magnetic field B pointing entirely in the positive x-direction. The diagram highlights the forces acting on the sides of the loop.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: According to Bohr's model of the hydrogen atom, an electron (charge e, mass m_e) revolves around the nucleus in a circular orbit of radius r with a uniform speed v. What is the equivalent magnetic dipole moment of this revolving electron?
questions.explanation: The revolving electron forms a current loop. Current I = e / T. Time period T = 2πr / v. So, I = ev / 2πr. Magnetic dipole moment M = I × A = (ev / 2πr) × (πr²) = e v r / 2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: An electron is moving in a region of space where a uniform electric field E and a uniform magnetic field B exist. The fields are mutually perpendicular, and the electron's velocity is perpendicular to both. If the electron passes through the region completely undeflected, what is its speed, given E = 10⁴ V/m and B = 0.05 T?
questions.explanation: For an electron to pass undeflected through crossed electric and magnetic fields, the electric and magnetic forces must exactly balance. qE = qvB implies v = E/B. Substituting E = 10⁴ V/m and B = 0.05 T yields v = 10⁴ / 0.05 = 2 × 10⁵ m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two identical circular coaxial loops of radius R are placed with their planes parallel and their centers separated by a distance R. Both loops carry the same steady current I in the same direction. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field at the point exactly midway between their centers on the common axis?
questions.explanation: Magnetic field on the axis of a circular loop at distance x is B = μ₀IR² / 2(R² + x²)^(3/2). For the midpoint, x = R/2. Fields from both loops add up: B_one = μ₀IR² / 2(R² + R²/4)^(3/2) = μ₀IR² / 2(5R²/4)^(3/2) = 4μ₀I / 5√5R. Total field B_total = 2 × B_one = 8μ₀I / 5√5R.
questions.imagePrompt: A 3D diagram showing two identical parallel circular loops of radius R, placed coaxially with their centers separated by a distance R. Both carry a current I in the same direction. A point P is marked exactly at the midpoint on the common axis between the two loops. Used in a physics exam to illustrate a Helmholtz coil-like setup.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A rigid, straight wire of mass m and length L carries a current I₁ and is suspended in mid-air in stable equilibrium just above another parallel, long straight wire fixed to the ground carrying a current I₂. What is the equilibrium height h of the suspended wire above the fixed wire? (Assume g is the acceleration due to gravity).
questions.explanation: For the suspended wire to be in stable equilibrium, the upward magnetic repulsive force must exactly balance the downward gravitational force. Magnetic force F_m = μ₀ I₁ I₂ L / 2πh. Equating forces: F_m = F_g => μ₀ I₁ I₂ L / 2πh = mg. Solving for h gives h = μ₀ I₁ I₂ L / 2πmg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A charged particle of mass m and charge q is projected with a velocity v at an angle of 60° to a uniform magnetic field B. The particle describes a helical path. If the pitch of the helix is p, what is the radius of the helical path in terms of the pitch?
questions.explanation: The pitch p = v_parallel * T = (v cosθ) * (2πm / qB). The radius r = m v_perp / qB = m v sinθ / qB. Taking the ratio: r/p = (m v sinθ / qB) / [(v cosθ) * (2πm / qB)] = tanθ / 2π. Substituting θ = 60° gives r/p = √3 / 2π, so r = √3p / 2π.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: A long solid cylindrical conductor of radius R carries a steady current I uniformly distributed over its cross-section. A long cylindrical cavity of radius R/2 is created inside the conductor, such that the axis of the cavity is parallel to the axis of the conductor and separated from it by a distance R/2. What is the magnitude of the magnetic field inside the cavity?
questions.explanation: Assuming I is the current of the full solid cylinder before the cavity, J = I / πR². By superposition, the magnetic field inside the cavity is uniform and given by B = (μ₀/2)(J × a), where a is the vector connecting the center of the main cylinder to the center of the cavity. Magnitude of B = μ₀Ja / 2. Given a = R/2, B = μ₀JR / 4. Substituting J gives B = μ₀(I/πR²)R / 4 = μ₀I / 4πR.
